page: Amazon Web Services c8i.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, and it operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance and top-tier capabilities in memory bandwidth and specialized compute tasks. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 103,797.54 and a PassMark CPU score of 106,933.38, both placing in the top tiers. Memory bandwidth tests show highly efficient cached read speeds of 7,683.33 GB/sec and uncached read speeds of 388.68 GB/sec. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance demonstrated exceptional throughput, including 171.2 million Redis SET operations per second and 154.92 GB/sec in static web serving. It also exhibits strong performance in LLM inference, particularly in prompt processing, reaching 320.04 tokens/sec for medium 7B models and 41.44 tokens/sec for large 70B models.

From a resource density perspective, the c8i.24xlarge offers high compute density with its dedicated 96 vCPUs and DDR5 memory, making it highly efficient for compute-bound workloads. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a tradeoff, requiring external network storage for data-heavy operations and limiting its suitability for heavy GPU-accelerated deep learning. Given its high multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operation scores, this instance is highly suited for high-performance computing, large-scale software compilation, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
